evidence.title: Weekly attendance exports for community arts courses
evidence.beneficiary: Course coordinators and instructors at eight independent community arts centers using a shared hosted administration service.
evidence.valued_outcome: Coordinators receive usable attendance files for the intended courses and week, with little manual work and no records from another center.
evidence.success_measure: Across the next 40 weekly exports, median coordinator handling time is at most 12 minutes, at least 95% contain the intended course set, and none contain another center’s participant records.

hard_constraints_with_source.text: Participant names must remain inside the existing private service and each center’s authorized workspace; no public external processing service may receive them.
The centers’ current spreadsheet import accepts one documented CSV schema, which must continue to be supported for the coming term.
A first bounded change has at most six engineer-days and must fit the existing monthly hosting allowance.
Instructors must remain able to enter attendance during ordinary class hours, including the interval when exports are prepared.

changeable_assumptions: Exports run on Sunday evening because that was the schedule requested by the first center.
The service treats a course’s current instructor assignment as the assignment relevant to any requested week.
evidence.incumbent_description: A scheduled job produces a CSV per center. A coordinator downloads it Monday, compares course names with a local schedule, and requests another export when something appears absent.

supplied_observations.text: In a sample of 40 exports, 32 contained the intended course set; eight prompted additional handling before coordinators used them.
Median handling time across all 40 files was 17 minutes. For 24 files from centers with unchanged course assignments, the median was seven minutes.
Six of the eight affected exports concerned courses whose instructor assignment changed during the requested week; two concerned recently renamed courses.
No cross-center rows were found in the 40 sampled files. This sample did not include the center that recently split one course into two.
Job execution took 40 to 75 seconds. Coordinators waited between 20 minutes and two working days for requested replacement files.
Four coordinators maintain separate schedules; three use the service’s course list; one keeps a printed timetable annotated during the week.
Service logs record job completion and row totals, but the sample includes no recordings of coordinator actions inside their spreadsheet application.

unmeasured_variables: The completeness and update timing of each local timetable.
Handling time attributable to checking, correcting, downloading, and importing separately.
available_resources: One engineer, a staging copy containing fabricated participants, and six consenting coordinators for two short sessions each.
Existing export logs and the documented CSV format.
evidence.evidence_provenance: authored synthetic case; observations stipulated not real empirical data

evidence.assessment: The incumbent can work with little handling: unchanged-assignment files had a seven-minute median. Overall, however, only 32/40 contained the intended course set and median handling was 17 minutes. Current-assignment semantics plausibly contribute to transition-week errors, but association is not causation. The two renamed-course cases limit an assignment-only explanation. Execution takes seconds while replacements take much longer; this does not establish that waiting accounts for measured handling time. No cross-center rows were observed, but the omitted split-course center limits that evidence. Neither the source of intended-course truth nor spreadsheet effort is established.

openings.claim: Requested-week course membership and stable course identity may diverge from current assignments or displayed names, causing some apparent omissions.
openings.delta: Distinguishes actual row exclusion from renamed courses that are present but unrecognized; reassignment alone cannot explain all affected files.
openings.prediction: If selection uses inappropriate current state, identical weekly attendance will produce different course coverage after a reassignment. If names cause recognition failures, stable course IDs will show coverage despite a reported omission.
openings.probe: In private staging, run fabricated unchanged, midweek-reassigned, renamed and split-course fixtures against an explicitly agreed weekly course set. Compare internal IDs and CSV rows, test a second center for leakage, and exercise attendance entry during export. Retain the documented CSV schema.
assumptions: Fixtures can define intended membership unambiguously.
These are diagnostic runs; historical-state availability and repair effort remain unknown.

openings.claim: Does excess active handling arise mainly from reconciling competing course lists, or from downloading and spreadsheet import?
openings.delta: Separates coordinator effort from replacement elapsed time and locates the next bounded intervention.
openings.prediction: A reconciliation-dominated account predicts more active checking and correction for transition cases; an import-dominated account predicts similar import effort across stable and transition cases.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators' two short sessions with fabricated stable and transition files, counterbalancing order. Time checking, correction, download and import separately; record replacement waiting separately and each coordinator's intended course set before inspection.
assumptions: Fabricated tasks approximate actual work.
Cap combined diagnostic work within six engineer-days and existing hosting; findings alone do not establish the next-40-export target.

evidence.assessment: Synthetic observations associate assignment changes and renames with errors; causation is unproven. These are alternative bounded hypotheses. Neither establishes split-course safety, implementation cost, or the success target.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: adapt museum accession tags, which separate identity from display labels, into a center-and-week course manifest. Cross identity continuity with coordinator reconciliation at the manifest-to-export interface: the confirmed course set drives the existing CSV generator.
openings.delta: Replace current-assignment selection with explicit weekly membership. Repurpose the existing course list as a reconciliation surface. Failed correspondence: one accession tag cannot describe a course splitting into two; splits require explicit weekly membership decisions. Changed assumptions: names and current instructors need not define historical inclusion.
openings.prediction: The hybrid reduces omissions after reassignment or renaming while avoiding a second full spreadsheet comparison; split cases may still require clarification.
openings.probe: Verify course-list provenance and available identifiers first. With fabricated reassignment, rename, and split cases, compare incumbent selection against manifest selection; measure intended-set accuracy and reconciliation time. Reject any cross-center rows or interrupted attendance entry.
assumptions: Stable center-scoped identity and historical membership are unverified enabling dependencies; do not infer missing history.
Coordinator reference schedules may be incomplete.
Private processing, unchanged CSV support, nonblocking reads, hosting cost, and six-day feasibility require verification.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: adapt parcel pickup notifications into private export-ready receipts. Cross authorized replacement requests with completion-triggered retrieval at a request-to-artifact interface.
openings.delta: Repurpose existing completion logs as readiness signals. Failed correspondence: job completion does not establish correct course contents. Changed assumption: replacement delivery can follow completion instead of an operator handoff.
openings.prediction: Replacement waiting falls if operator handoffs cause the delay; active handling and course accuracy may remain unchanged.
openings.probe: Verify whether logs can bind an authorized center/week request to its exact private CSV. Across two short sessions per consenting coordinator, share the session budget with A1 and separately time checking, requesting, waiting, downloading, and importing. Subsequently assess 40 exports against all stated success measures.
assumptions: Request/artifact identifiers, authorization checks, and completion hooks are unverified dependencies.
Use unchanged CSVs within authorized workspaces; bound retries and verify concurrency, hosting, and six-day feasibility.

critiques.assumption: An agreed weekly manifest supplies sufficiently reliable intended-course truth to validate selection and reduce handling.
critiques.limitation: D1-O6 supplies heterogeneous references, while timetable completeness and update timing are unmeasured. Agreement with a manifest could therefore reproduce a shared omission. Fabricated fixtures establish behavior against stipulated truth, not the reliability of real manifests. This supports an evidence gap, not a finding that coordinators' schedules are wrong.
critiques.opening: Test reference disagreement and uncertainty explicitly before treating manifest confirmation as a correctness check.
critiques.comparison: Stable identity addresses renaming but cannot determine split-week membership. Coordinator reconciliation supplies week-specific intent but may be incomplete and costly. Their useful interaction requires explicit treatment of unresolved membership.
critiques.probe: Proposed only: inject stale-reference and split-course disagreements into fabricated tasks, including a case where both references omit the same intended course.

openings.claim: Use stable center-scoped identities with discrepancy-focused weekly reconciliation and an explicit unresolved-membership state.
openings.delta: Extend A1's confirmed manifest with reference provenance and unresolved decisions; prevent unresolved cases from being counted as verified usable exports. Include deliberately shared omissions in assessment.
openings.prediction: Relative to identity continuity alone, explicit decisions may resolve split and reassignment ambiguity. Relative to full coordinator reconciliation alone, identity matching may reduce repeated name checks. The interaction concentrates review on semantic changes. Failure boundary: jointly stale references can hide discrepancies; unresolved cases can increase handling or delay usable delivery.
openings.probe: Proposed, not performed: share the six coordinators' existing two-session budget across identity-only, reconciliation-only and combined fabricated tasks, counterbalancing order. Establish intended sets independently in task specifications. Measure correctness, unresolved cases and active handling; retain unresolved cases in outcome accounting. Test center isolation and concurrent attendance entry. First assess existing identifiers plus a minimal private prototype; stop expansion if six engineer-days or hosting allowance cannot hold. Subsequently measure the original next-40-export target.
assumptions: Processing remains private and the documented CSV remains supported.
Historical membership is not inferred from missing records.
Discrepancy detection does not establish reference completeness; fabricated results cannot establish field success.

openings.claim: Weekly membership or renamed identities may explain omissions; reassignment alone is insufficient.
openings.discriminator: Actual exclusion versus present but unrecognized courses.
openings.probe: Compare agreed sets, IDs and CSV rows across fabricated stable, reassigned, renamed and split courses; test isolation and concurrent attendance.
openings.uncertainty: Association is not causation; historical records and fixture intent require verification. Omitted split-center sampling limits safety evidence.

openings.claim: Locate active effort in reconciliation, correction, download or import.
openings.discriminator: Transition-specific checking versus similar import effort; elapsed replacement waiting is separate.
openings.probe: Counterbalance fabricated stable/transition tasks; time stages separately and record intended sets before inspection.
openings.uncertainty: Local reference completeness and real spreadsheet behavior are unmeasured; fabricated tasks may misrepresent field work.

openings.claim: Stable center-scoped identity plus discrepancy-focused weekly reconciliation could drive existing CSV selection; preserve reference provenance and unresolved membership.
openings.discriminator: Identity handles renames; explicit intent handles splits; unresolved and jointly stale references prevent confirmation from proving completeness.
openings.probe: Compare identity-only, reconciliation-only and combined tasks with independent intended sets, stale references, shared omissions and splits; measure accuracy, handling and unresolved outcomes.
openings.uncertainty: Identifiers, historical membership, references and bounded implementation are unverified; do not infer missing history or count unresolved exports as verified usable.

openings.claim: Private export-ready receipts could connect authorized replacement requests to completion-triggered retrieval.
openings.discriminator: Operator-handoff waiting may fall while accuracy and active effort remain unchanged.
openings.probe: Verify exact center/week request-to-CSV binding and completion hooks; time request, waiting and retrieval separately.
openings.uncertainty: Authorization, identifiers, hooks, retries, concurrency and feasibility remain unverified; completion does not prove correct contents.

lineage.reason: Provenance, unresolved decisions and shared omissions retained.

evidence.decision: Prioritize diagnostics before choosing implementation. Share six coordinators’ two-session budget; keep names private within authorized workspaces, documented CSV support, concurrent attendance, six engineer-days and existing hosting. Evidence is synthetic; subsequently require next-40 median handling ≤12 minutes, ≥95% intended course sets and zero cross-center records.

openings.claim: Replay weekly selection: current assignments may exclude courses; renamed rows may instead escape recognition.
openings.discriminator: Coverage changes after reassignment versus stable IDs revealing present renamed rows.
openings.probe: Compare fabricated unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split cases against agreed sets and internal IDs.
openings.uncertainty: Fixture truth is stipulated; historical availability and repair effort unknown.

openings.claim: Observe whether reconciliation or download/import drives active handling; replacement waiting is separate.
openings.discriminator: Transition-specific checking versus similar import effort across cases.
openings.probe: Counterbalance fabricated stable/transition tasks; record intended sets before inspection and time each activity separately.
openings.uncertainty: Fabricated work may poorly approximate actual practice.

openings.claim: Use stable identities plus provenance-aware, discrepancy-focused weekly reconciliation to drive CSV membership; explicitly preserve unresolved decisions, including splits.
openings.discriminator: Combined identity/reconciliation improves accuracy or effort over either alone.
openings.probe: Verify identifiers/history; compare three approaches with independently specified sets, stale references, shared omissions and splits. Count unresolved cases and handling.
openings.uncertainty: Missing history cannot be inferred; jointly stale references hide omissions. Unresolved decisions can delay delivery; stop expansion beyond budget.

openings.claim: Bind authorized replacement requests to exact center/week CSVs and completion-triggered private receipts; operator handoffs may cause waiting.
openings.discriminator: Waiting falls while accuracy and active handling may remain unchanged.
openings.probe: Verify request/artifact bindings and hooks; separately time request, waiting and retrieval; bound retries.
openings.uncertainty: Bindings and authorization unverified; completion proves no content correctness.

lineage.reason: Provenance, unresolved membership and shared-omission boundary retained.

evidence.decision: Diagnose before choosing intervention. Synthetic evidence establishes no causation. Share six coordinators' two sessions; cap combined work at six engineer-days and existing monthly hosting. Names stay within private service/authorized workspaces; preserve documented CSV and concurrent attendance entry. Test isolation, including split center. Field success requires next 40 exports: median handling <=12 minutes, intended sets >=95%, zero cross-center records.

evidence.title: Assembling configurable desktop stationery organizers
evidence.beneficiary: A small workshop packing desktop organizers and customers arranging stationery for classes and home studios.
evidence.valued_outcome: Customers can put the supplied organizer into their ordered arrangement without replacement parts, while the workshop completes orders within its available working time.
evidence.success_measure: For a 60-unit pilot, at least 98% of orders contain every required component, median workshop assembly and packing time is at most eight minutes, and at least 90% of customers achieve their ordered arrangement unaided.

hard_constraints_with_source.text: The assembled organizer must fit a 30 by 20 centimeter footprint and hold the same specified stationery assortment as the current product.
Customers must be able to dismantle and rearrange the supplied partitions; permanent bonds between partitions and the base are prohibited.
The workshop may spend at most 500 currency units initially and add no more than 0.40 units to recurring material cost per order.
Orders already accepted must retain their selected compartment counts and exterior color, and the existing 60-unit delivery date remains fixed.

changeable_assumptions: All organizers are fully assembled before packing, although the sales description promises an organizer with rearrangeable compartments.
Parts are currently grouped by shape in open bins shared by both workshop staff.
evidence.incumbent_description: Two workers select die-cut board parts, insert partitions into base slots, check the order slip, and pack the assembled product with a diagram showing three possible layouts.

supplied_observations.text: The last 60 orders included 22 three-compartment, 26 four-compartment, and 12 six-compartment layouts; ten orders used a less common exterior color.
Median assembly and packing time was 11 minutes, with a range of six to 24 minutes; the observation combined both activities.
Five customers reported a missing or incorrect partition. Two reports included photographs; the remaining three were resolved from written descriptions.
In a ten-person observed unpacking session, seven achieved their ordered arrangement unaided within ten minutes; three asked where a short partition belonged.
Seventeen of 120 sampled partitions needed a second insertion attempt. Recorded widths overlapped between those parts and parts inserted on the first attempt.
Both workers completed repeated three-compartment orders in seven to nine minutes. Mixed-layout batches contained all six orders that took over 18 minutes.
No damage claims were recorded for this batch. Packaging occupied 28 liters per ten organizers, measured before dispatch.

unmeasured_variables: How often customers alter their arrangement after the initial unpacking.
Separate time spent selecting parts, inserting partitions, checking contents, and packing.
available_resources: Existing cutting templates, two workers, one bench, spare board for 15 samples, and ten willing customer participants.
evidence.evidence_provenance: authored synthetic case; observations stipulated not real empirical data

evidence.assessment: The incumbent supplies removable partitions already assembled and checks an order slip, providing an opportunity to verify the requested configuration. Repeated three-compartment orders approach the time target (D2-O6), so assembly is not uniformly slow. Mixed batches contain every extreme delay, but layout complexity and switching are confounded. Missing/incorrect-part reports and unpacking confusion show checks and the generic diagram do not reliably secure the outcome (D2-O3/O4). Concrete limitation: insertion-retry widths overlap first-pass widths (D2-O5), weakening a simple width-only account without excluding slot fit, orientation or handling. These are synthetic observations, not established causal explanations.

openings.claim: Preparing an order-specific parts set and checking it against the selected layout before insertion may reduce mixed-batch selection mistakes and delays.
openings.delta: Replace repeated shared-bin selection during assembly with a bounded per-order selection and verification step; retain full assembly and reversible joints.
openings.prediction: Within the same layout and worker, prepared sets reduce selection/checking time or detected component discrepancies; insertion time may remain unchanged. Unchanged selection performance would weaken this account.
openings.probe: Use spare-board samples in counterbalanced matched runs, recording selection, insertion, checking and packing separately. Include set preparation in total time and inspect final parts/count/color. Gate adoption on measured cost limits and available time before the fixed delivery date.
assumptions: Layout-specific required parts can be derived from existing templates and order slips.
Preparation does not consume more time or bench capacity than it saves; cost and schedule feasibility remain unmeasured.

openings.claim: A diagram of the customer's ordered layout explicitly locating the short partition may improve unaided arrangement.
openings.delta: Replace the three-layout diagram with order-specific placement guidance, without changing components or rearrangeability.
openings.prediction: Customers receiving the specific diagram make fewer short-partition placement errors and achieve their ordered layout more often; persistent failures suggest guidance alone is insufficient.
openings.probe: Assign the ten willing participants across existing versus specific diagrams, balancing layout and prior exposure. Verify complete kits beforehand; record unaided success and placement errors. Treat this small comparison as directional evidence; verify production outcomes in the 60-unit pilot.
assumptions: Diagram preparation and printing fit both cost caps and the fixed deadline.
Previously observed participants may have learned the layouts, limiting generalization.

evidence.assessment: Synthetic observations support investigating selection and arrangement ambiguity, but do not establish the source of missing parts or insertion retries. This proposed hybrid remains unvalidated against time, cost, delivery, capacity and customer-success requirements.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: an order-specific reusable packing map can carry each supplied partition in a labeled outline and then unfold beside the base as an assembly guide. This moves inventory checking and short-part placement guidance into the shipping artifact, permitting customer assembly while retaining removable partitions.
openings.delta: Parent mechanisms are a physical inventory silhouette and a spatial assembly template. Their interaction makes each carried part correspond to its destination in the selected arrangement. Mixed-layout complexity becomes information: an unmatched outline or leftover part exposes a discrepancy. A speculative extension would prevent the carrier closing unless every required part occupies its matching position; dependencies include shape discrimination, reversible retention and a closure that cannot be defeated by an empty pocket. The presently testable partial capability is visible mismatch detection using hand-cut or drawn maps.
openings.prediction: Compared with the incumbent diagram, mapped kits should reduce short-part placement questions and expose planted missing or wrong partitions before dispatch. Workshop time should fall only if map preparation, loading and checking cost less time than the removed assembly.
openings.probe: Use spare board to prototype maps for the three accepted compartment counts. Test detectable omissions and substitutions with both workers, separately timing selection, loading, checking and packing. Assign ten participants to mapped kits or incumbent presentation using comparable layouts; record unaided arrangement, questions and completion. Check capacity, rearrangement, color, actual material costs and preparation time before committing the fixed-date pilot. Pilot targets remain at least 59 complete orders, median workshop time at most eight minutes and at least 54 unaided customer arrangements.
assumptions: Existing packaging can be adapted within 500 initial and 0.40 recurring cost limits.
Map production fits the existing delivery schedule.
Partitions remain undamaged and detachable.
Failure boundary: visually similar wrong parts, incorrect maps or loose contents can defeat the visible check; closure interlocking is speculative.

critiques.assumption: Agreement between parts, packing map and destination diagram establishes agreement with the accepted order.
critiques.limitation: A wrong map could accept a complete set for another layout and teach that same wrong arrangement. D2-O3/O4 establish discrepancies and confusion, but do not establish this common-source failure. Geometric outlines also need not distinguish exterior color.
critiques.opening: Check order identity independently before using the map to check physical completeness and guide placement.
critiques.comparison: The inventory silhouette detects absent or mismatched shapes; the spatial template explains destinations. Their coupling transfers one correspondence from packing to assembly, but also propagates a wrong correspondence. Z1 and Z2 can share this vulnerability if both inherit the same mistaken layout selection. A closure interlock adds physical occupancy enforcement but cannot establish that the map represents the accepted order.
critiques.probe: Deliberately swap otherwise complete layout maps between sample orders, including the same layout with a wrong exterior color. Compare shape-only checks with independent order-slip checks; these are proposed challenges, not observed failures.

openings.claim: An independently verified order-specific map may combine inventory checking and placement guidance while catching configurations that are internally consistent but wrong for the order.
openings.delta: Before loading, the second worker checks the map against the original order slip for compartment count, component requirements and exterior color; the packing worker then checks physical contents against the verified map. Both checking times count toward workshop time.
openings.prediction: Relative to A1, this should detect more swapped-map errors; relative to Z1, the retained map should help placement; relative to Z2, physical matching should expose omissions. Shared mistaken specifications or rushed second checks defeat the interaction.
openings.probe: Reuse up to 15 samples across counterbalanced challenged checks by both workers. Include map preparation and both checks in total time. Use ten participants for directional unaided-arrangement evidence. Measure actual costs and delivery feasibility before adoption; only the 60-order pilot can assess its specified completeness, time and customer-success targets.
assumptions: Original slips accurately preserve accepted choices.
Independent checking remains practical with two workers and one bench.
The unchanged footprint, stationery capacity, removable partitions, accepted counts/colors, cost caps and delivery date remain mandatory.

openings.claim: Prepare and verify order-specific parts sets before insertion.
openings.discriminator: Matched layouts/workers improve selection or checking; insertion may remain unchanged.
openings.probe: Counterbalance sample runs; separately time preparation, selection, insertion, checks and packing; inspect count/color.
openings.uncertainty: Mixed-layout switching and complexity are confounded; preparation may consume saved time or bench capacity. Retry widths overlap, weakening width-only explanations.

openings.claim: Ordered-layout diagrams explicitly locate the short partition.
openings.discriminator: Fewer placement errors and more unaided arrangements than generic diagrams.
openings.probe: Compare diagrams across ten participants with complete kits, balanced layouts and prior exposure.
openings.uncertainty: Guidance may be insufficient; prior learning and small samples limit generalization. Preparation/printing feasibility is unknown.

openings.claim: A reusable carrier maps each partition outline to its destination, combining visible inventory checks with customer assembly guidance; independently verify its count, component requirements and color against the original slip before loading.
openings.discriminator: Matching exposes omissions; destinations aid placement; independent order verification catches internally consistent swapped maps that physical occupancy alone cannot.
openings.probe: Reuse up to 15 samples for worker challenges with omissions, substitutions, swapped layouts and wrong colors; time map preparation/loading/both checks/packing; compare customer arrangements.
openings.uncertainty: Similar shapes, wrong maps, loose contents, shared mistaken specifications or rushed checks defeat checks. Slip accuracy, detachable retention, damage, two-worker/one-bench feasibility and time savings remain unverified. Closure interlocking is speculative and cannot verify order identity.

lineage.reason: Retains carrier-to-destination coupling and speculative closure boundary.
Retains independent order verification and comparative challenges.

evidence.decision: All are unvalidated synthetic hypotheses. Preserve 30x20 cm footprint, stationery capacity, removable partitions, accepted counts/colors and fixed delivery date; cap initial spending at 500 and recurring addition at 0.40/order. Measure actual costs and total workshop time before adoption. Rearrangement frequency and separate task times are unknown. Ten participants provide directional evidence; the 60-order pilot must achieve at least 59 complete orders, median time <=8 minutes and at least 54 unaided arrangements.

openings.claim: Prepare and verify order-specific parts sets before insertion; reduced shared-bin selection may reduce mixed-batch mistakes and delays.
openings.discriminator: Within matched layout/worker, selection/checking improves; insertion may remain unchanged.
openings.probe: Counterbalance samples; separately time selection, insertion, checking, packing, including preparation; inspect final parts/count/color.
openings.uncertainty: Required sets must be derivable from templates/slips; preparation, bench use, cost and deadline may erase savings. Complexity versus switching remains confounded.

openings.claim: Replace generic diagrams with ordered-layout guidance locating the short partition; clearer destinations may improve unaided arrangement.
openings.discriminator: Fewer placement errors and more ordered arrangements; persistent failures weaken guidance alone.
openings.probe: Compare diagrams among ten participants, balancing layout/exposure and verifying complete kits first.
openings.uncertainty: Prior learning limits generalization; preparation/printing cost and deadline feasibility unmeasured.

openings.claim: A reusable labeled packing map carries partitions then unfolds into destination guidance, permitting customer assembly. Independently verify map requirements/count/color against original slips before physical matching: silhouettes expose omissions, spatial correspondence guides placement, independent identity checking catches internally consistent wrong orders.
openings.discriminator: Detect planted omissions/substitutions and swapped maps/colors; reduce placement questions. Time falls only if preparation/loading/checks cost less than removed assembly.
openings.probe: Reuse up to 15 samples for three accepted counts, counterbalanced worker challenges; time preparation and both checks. Compare mapped/incumbent presentation with ten participants; verify capacity, removability, damage, costs and delivery.
openings.uncertainty: Accurate slips and practical two-worker/one-bench checks required. Similar parts, wrong maps, loose contents or rushed/shared mistakes defeat checks. Closure interlock parked: occupancy enforcement depends on shape discrimination/reversible retention and resisting empty-pocket defeat; cannot establish order identity.

lineage.reason: Inventory/destination coupling retained; speculative closure parked.

evidence.decision: Synthetic hypotheses only. Require 30x20 cm footprint, same stationery capacity, removable partitions/no permanent bonds, initial cost <=500, recurring addition <=0.40/order, accepted counts/colors and fixed delivery date. Ten-person comparisons are directional; assess 60-unit pilot: >=59 complete orders, median workshop time <=8 minutes, >=54 unaided arrangements. Gate adoption on measured feasibility.

available_resources: Existing cutting templates, two workers, one bench, spare board for 15 samples, and ten willing customer participants.
evidence.evidence_provenance: authored synthetic case; observations stipulated not real empirical data

evidence.assessment: The incumbent supplies an assembled, rearrangeable product with an order check. Preassembly could spare customers insertion work, but that benefit is unmeasured. D2-O6 limits the claim that assembly inherently exceeds eight minutes: repeated three-compartment orders took seven to nine minutes, while mixed batches contained every extreme delay. Layout complexity and switching remain confounded, and D2-O2 combines activities. Missing-part reports and short-partition questions indicate separate completeness and interpretation risks; neither their causes nor pilot success are established.

openings.claim: Reusable order-specific staging of all required parts before insertion may reduce selection/checking delays and component errors during mixed-layout work.
openings.delta: Replace direct picking from shared shape bins with a counted kit tied to the existing order slip, including exterior color, while retaining assembly and the final check.
openings.prediction: If switching and selection are important causes, staging will reduce total time and audited content errors, especially after layout changes; insertion time need not change.
openings.probe: Use twelve sample builds in six matched pairs spanning the three layouts, counterbalancing worker and method order. Compare incumbent picking with staging; record selection including kit preparation, insertion, checking, packing, and final completeness separately. Record transitions and color. Include staging setup cost and bench occupancy; adopt only within both cost limits and the fixed delivery schedule.
assumptions: Reusable staging fits the single bench and available spare board.
Any preparation savings exceed staging labor; this is unproven.

openings.claim: An order-specific drawing identifying the short partition may improve unaided arrangement success.
openings.delta: Annotate the existing order slip with the selected arrangement and short-partition position, leaving components and reversible connections unchanged.
openings.prediction: With independently verified complete kits, short-partition placement questions decrease relative to the existing diagram.
openings.probe: Randomly assign ten willing participants to five existing-diagram and five annotated-slip trials on matched unfamiliar layouts. Record unaided completion, short-partition errors, questions, and time; include annotation labor in workshop totals. Treat this as screening, then verify all three success measures during the 60-unit pilot.
assumptions: The drawing is accurate and legible.
Annotation labor remains compatible with the time target and delivery date.

evidence.assessment: Two unvalidated artifact/interface hypotheses. Observations suggest selection and orientation opportunities but establish neither error causes nor achievable savings. Both require cost, capacity and schedule checks before adoption.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: an order-specific board carrier replaces part of the worker contents check and customer layout interpretation. Each required partition occupies an outlined position; adjacent placement marks map it to the ordered arrangement.
openings.delta: Hybrid parents are a completeness stencil and an assembly map. Mixed-layout variation becomes a visible empty position, overlap or unmatched mark. A speculative carrier would encode every valid kit and arrangement automatically; dependencies are a verified layout-to-parts mapping and distinguishable part outlines. Test a manually traced partial capability first.
openings.prediction: The carrier reduces unnoticed missing/wrong parts and short-partition questions, particularly during mixed-layout work.
openings.probe: Use spare-board mockups for all three counts, counterbalance mixed-order packing against current practice, and deliberately seed omissions and substitutions. Record detection and separate selection/checking/packing times; compare unaided layout success with ten participants.
assumptions: Failure boundary: same-outline incompatible parts or an incorrect order map can pass; exterior color needs an explicit matching cue.
Carrier fits existing packaging; production cost stays within 0.40 per order and 500 initially, with delivery unchanged. Retain original functional components and reversible joints.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: a reversible compliant lead-in with a visible seating witness transfers alignment guidance into the partition/base interface.
openings.delta: Hybrid parents are an elastic guide and a displacement indicator: insertion resistance deflects the guide, exposing a misalignment cue before seating. A speculative self-correcting joint requires controlled board stiffness, safe elastic travel and load-bearing seating; a marked sacrificial guide tests the partial sensing capability.
openings.prediction: If misalignment contributes, visible guide deflection predicts repeat attempts and guidance reduces them; overlapping widths alone cannot establish this.
openings.probe: Compare current, witness-only and guide-plus-witness sample joints. Record attempts, force, cue accuracy and damage; repeatedly dismantle, rearrange and load successful samples with the specified assortment.
assumptions: Failure boundary: excessive force, moisture or fatigue defeats elastic guidance; misleading cues reject the design.
Preserve footprint, capacity, counts and exterior color. Tooling, recurring cost and implementation time must meet the fixed constraints.

critiques.assumption: An outlined carrier can support both workshop completeness checking and customer arrangement guidance under the incumbent assembled handoff.
critiques.limitation: The supplied incumbent is packed assembled. A1 does not specify how a customer reads the carrier after parts leave its outlined positions. A reusable staging aid and a shipped carrier also have different cost and bench implications. No supplied observation establishes that either is feasible.
critiques.opening: Separate the reusable physical checking surface from its portable arrangement key, preserving an explicit correspondence between them.
critiques.comparison: Z1 supplies counted staging; Z2 supplies a customer drawing; A1 couples both on one carrier. A reusable mat plus matching annotated order slip could retain their interaction without requiring a carrier in every shipment. The shared mapping can also propagate one error through both checks.
critiques.probe: Compare coupled and independently prepared staging/drawing combinations, counting all preparation and transfer labor. Independently verify the mapping against an actual assembled sample before using it.

openings.claim: A reusable order-specific staging mat paired with a matching arrangement key on the existing slip may connect workshop component verification to customer reconstruction while retaining preassembly.
openings.delta: Keep A1's outlined positions at the bench; transfer only the arrangement key to the slip. Include selected exterior color and a distinct short-partition cue.
openings.prediction: Relative to Z1 alone, the key should improve reconstruction; relative to Z2 alone, the mat should expose omissions. Relative to A1, reuse may lower recurring material cost, but copying labor may erase time savings. Incorrect mappings or indistinguishable incompatible parts defeat both channels.
openings.probe: First manually verify one layout's mapping using existing templates and a sample; automatic mapping remains unsupported. Screen incumbent, mat-only, key-only and coupled versions within 15 samples, including seeded errors. Use ten participants for exploratory reconstruction trials; confirm thresholds in the 60-unit pilot only if costs and schedule permit.
assumptions: Footprint, capacity, reversible partitions, ordered counts and colors remain unchanged.
Initial cost stays at most 500, added recurring materials at most 0.40 per order, and delivery remains fixed.
Single-bench occupancy and annotation labor are included in timing; all probes remain proposed.

openings.claim: Counted order/color kits may reduce mixed-layout selection errors and delays while retaining preassembly.
openings.discriminator: Savings concentrate after layout switches; insertion need not improve.
openings.probe: Twelve builds, six matched pairs; counterbalance workers/order. Separate staging, selection, insertion, checking, packing; audit completeness, bench occupancy and costs.
openings.uncertainty: Layout complexity confounds switching; staging preparation may erase savings.

openings.claim: An ordered-layout drawing identifying the short partition may improve unaided arrangement.
openings.discriminator: Complete kits isolate interpretation from omissions.
openings.probe: Five existing-diagram versus five annotated-slip participants on matched unfamiliar layouts; measure completion, questions, errors, time and annotation labor.
openings.uncertainty: Legibility and labor feasibility remain untested.

openings.claim: An outlined carrier combines completeness stencil and placement map.
openings.discriminator: Empty positions or unmatched marks expose errors while mapping parts to arrangement.
openings.probe: Mock up three counts; seed omissions/substitutions; compare mixed-order work and customer reconstruction.
openings.uncertainty: Same-outline incompatibilities, wrong maps and color mismatches can pass; post-preassembly readability, packaging fit and costs are unresolved. Automatic mapping is unsupported.

openings.claim: A reversible elastic lead-in with seating witness may guide insertion through visible deflection.
openings.discriminator: Deflection predicts misalignment and repeat attempts.
openings.probe: Compare current, witness-only and guided joints; measure attempts, force, cue accuracy, damage, repeated dismantling and specified loads.
openings.uncertainty: Overlapping widths establish no cause; stiffness, travel, seating, moisture and fatigue may defeat guidance.

openings.claim: Reusable outlined staging plus a matching portable slip key retains carrier correspondence under preassembly.
openings.discriminator: Compare incumbent, mat-only, key-only and coupled versions, including independently prepared mappings.
openings.probe: Verify mapping against an assembled sample; screen within fifteen samples and ten participants; count transfer labor.
openings.uncertainty: Shared mapping errors propagate; indistinguishable parts defeat checks; reuse savings may disappear.

evidence.decision: Proposed screens, synthetic evidence only. Preserve 30×20 cm footprint, specified assortment capacity, dismantlable/rearrangeable partitions without permanent bonds, accepted counts/colors and fixed delivery. Cap initial spending at 500 and added materials at 0.40/order. Include all labor and single-bench occupancy. Pilot: 60 units, ≥98% complete, median assembly/packing ≤8 minutes, ≥90% unaided arrangement; screens cannot establish these thresholds.

openings.claim: Counted reusable staging mat plus matching portable order-slip key links component verification to reconstruction; include color and short-partition cues. Independently verify the layout-to-parts mapping on an assembled sample.
openings.discriminator: Mat-only should expose omissions; key-only should improve reconstruction; coupling should provide both, unless copying labor erases selection/transition savings.
openings.probe: Screen incumbent, mat-only, key-only and coupled versus independently prepared variants within 15 samples; counterbalance workers/transitions, seed errors, and use ten participants. Separately time preparation, selection, insertion, checking, packing and transfer.
openings.uncertainty: Bench fit and savings unproven; complexity/switching confounded. Shared erroneous maps or indistinguishable incompatible parts defeat checks; automatic mapping unsupported.

openings.claim: Outlined board carrier combines a completeness stencil with adjacent arrangement marks, replacing some checking and interpretation only with verified maps and distinguishable outlines.
openings.discriminator: Empty positions, overlaps or unmatched marks should reveal omissions/substitutions and reduce short-partition questions.
openings.probe: Manually trace three-count mockups; counterbalance mixed-order packing, seed errors, measure detection and separate selection/checking/packing times; test ten participants.
openings.uncertainty: Same-outline incompatibility or incorrect maps can pass. Customer readability after preassembly, packaging fit, explicit color matching and recurring carrier cost remain gates.

openings.claim: Reversible compliant lead-in plus seating witness uses resistance-induced elastic deflection to expose misalignment before seating; requires controlled board stiffness, safe travel and load-bearing seating.
openings.discriminator: Deflection should predict repeat attempts; guidance should reduce them. Overlapping widths establish no cause.
openings.probe: Compare current, witness-only and guide-plus-witness joints; record attempts, force, cue accuracy and damage; repeatedly dismantle, rearrange and load with specified stationery.
openings.uncertainty: Excess force, moisture or fatigue may defeat guidance; stop for misleading cues, damage or failed constraint checks.

lineage.reason: Counted staging and transition-sensitive timing preserved.
Portable short-partition drawing and customer comparison preserved.
Mat/key correspondence, independent verification and shared-error risk preserved.

evidence.decision: Proposed screens only; synthetic observations prove no mechanism. Preserve 30x20 cm footprint, specified capacity, reversible partitions without permanent bonds, accepted counts/colors and fixed delivery. Gate initial cost <=500 and added recurring materials <=0.40/order. Confirm no-replacement outcomes in the 60-unit pilot: >=98% complete, median total <=8 minutes, >=90% unaided arrangement; small screens cannot establish these.

evidence.title: Coordinating practice in a volunteer language circle
evidence.beneficiary: Adult participants in a free conversational language circle and the volunteers who coordinate weekly practice.
evidence.valued_outcome: Participants obtain useful speaking practice at their current level and can prepare for the next session without excessive coordination effort.
evidence.success_measure: Over six sessions, at least 80% of attending participants report ten or more minutes of useful speaking practice, at least 85% correctly identify their next preparation task, and volunteer coordination stays below 90 minutes per week.

hard_constraints_with_source.text: Participation remains free, and no learner may be excluded for missing a prior session or declining to disclose a proficiency label publicly.
The circle has one room for 75 minutes each Wednesday and no additional paid facilitator time.
Participants must be able to obtain preparation information without a smartphone or personal online account.
The group’s purpose remains conversational practice; success may not be substituted with formal examination scores or completion of unrelated assignments.

changeable_assumptions: The same topic sheet is currently distributed to everyone regardless of previous attendance.
Participants choose their conversation partners after a whole-group opening activity.
evidence.incumbent_description: A volunteer selects a weekly topic, prints prompts, and sends an optional group message. After introductions, participants practice in pairs and later share a short exchange with the room.

supplied_observations.text: Attendance over six sessions was 18, 11, 21, 15, 12, and 20. Nine people attended at least five sessions; 17 attended only once or twice.
Anonymous exit slips from 72 attendances reported ten useful speaking minutes on 49 occasions; 14 slips reported fewer, and nine left that question blank.
Forty-eight of the 72 slips named the intended next preparation task. Twelve named an earlier task, and twelve supplied no task.
Volunteer coordination took between 70 and 135 minutes per week, including printing, answering messages, choosing topics, and arranging room access.
In two sessions, pair formation took eight and 13 minutes. Four participants changed partners after the first prompt in each session.
Seven frequent attendees described the repeated session structure as helpful. Five occasional attendees reported difficulty entering a conversation already familiar to their partner.
The volunteer counted nine participants who regularly used printed information only. Speaking time was not directly timed, and exit slips were not linked across weeks.

unmeasured_variables: Participants’ definitions of useful practice and the distribution of speaking time within pairs.
Reasons for irregular attendance and time spent on each coordination activity.
available_resources: Two volunteers who alternate weeks, a printer, existing topic sheets, movable chairs, and permission for anonymous session observation.
evidence.evidence_provenance: authored synthetic case; observations stipulated not real empirical data

evidence.assessment: The incumbent provides free, repeatable conversational practice and printed access; seven frequent attendees explicitly valued its structure (H3-O6). Predictability may reduce their orientation burden, but this is a hypothesis. The concrete limiting observation is five occasional attendees struggling to enter conversations already familiar to partners (H3-O6): the same continuity may help some while hindering others. Slow pairing and partner changes suggest friction without establishing its cause (H3-O5). Available slips show 49/72 reporting sufficient useful practice and 48/72 identifying preparation correctly; missing and unlinked responses prevent a complete attendance-level assessment (H3-O2,O3,O7). Coordination sometimes exceeds 90 minutes (H3-O4).

openings.claim: Unequal familiarity with the conversation, rather than proficiency mismatch alone, may explain some difficult pair starts.
openings.delta: Retain the valued session structure while testing whether a shared starting point improves entry for occasional attendees.
openings.prediction: Pairs using a fresh, self-contained prompt and brief mutual introduction will start reciprocal speaking sooner and report more useful practice, especially where prior topic familiarity differs.
openings.probe: Within a session, randomly offer consenting pairs either the usual prompt or a fresh self-contained equivalent with a one-minute introduction. Privately record topic familiarity without proficiency labels; anonymously observe time to reciprocal speaking and each partner's speaking minutes, then collect usefulness reports. Keep both activities inside 75 minutes and record volunteer preparation time.
assumptions: Equivalent prompts can be prepared within the weekly coordination ceiling.
Familiarity can be reported privately; unequal proficiency and prompt differences remain alternative explanations.

openings.claim: Some preparation errors may reflect confusion between current and earlier task information.
openings.delta: Test task identification at paper handoff before attributing errors to irregular attendance or motivation.
openings.prediction: A clearly dated paper card naming the next session and one preparation task will reduce earlier-task answers relative to the existing presentation.
openings.probe: Give consenting attendees the same next task in either existing format or a reusable dated-card format. Ask privately which task and session it refers to; correct every misunderstanding and provide the dated information to everyone afterward. Count earlier-task and blank answers separately and log printing, explanation, and message time.
assumptions: Immediate identification may not predict later recall.
The card is available without an account and does not make preparation a condition of participation.

evidence.assessment: The supplied observations suggest difficulties with conversation entry and preparation continuity, but establish neither their causes nor the distribution of speaking time. Both capabilities below are hypotheses; neither is demonstrated to meet the six-session targets.

openings.claim: A self-calibrating conversation could let partners use different amounts of support while discussing the same fresh prompt, without declaring proficiency or relying on previous attendance.
openings.delta: Speculative capability: continuously adjust each person's conversational challenge. Dependencies: accessible entry prompts, independently usable scaffolds, turn allocation, and a reliable signal that challenge remains useful. Presently testable partial capability: reuse existing sheets with optional sentence starters and extension prompts; alternate speaker roles for two six-minute turns before jointly choosing whether to change support.
openings.prediction: If unequal entry difficulty or turn allocation contributes to low usefulness, the supported rounds should increase both partners' reported useful minutes and reduce the within-pair speaking-time gap. Unchanged usefulness despite more balanced speech would weaken that explanation.
openings.probe: Within a session, alternate the order of usual and supported rounds across pairs using comparable fresh prompts. Anonymous observation records each partner's speaking time; brief round slips record useful minutes and entry difficulty. Log preparation time and include it in weekly coordination totals.
assumptions: Scaffolds can be adapted within existing volunteer time.
Participants can select support without public proficiency labels.
Balanced speaking does not necessarily mean useful practice.

openings.claim: An attendance-independent preparation packet could make the next task recoverable after missed sessions through calendar dates alone.
openings.delta: Speculative capability: preserve preparation continuity without tracking learners. Dependencies: a stable six-session topic sequence, self-contained tasks, unambiguous dates, and printed distribution. Testable partial capability: provide six dated, detachable preparation cards made from existing topics, with spare packets available at every session.
openings.prediction: If stale task information contributes to errors, dated packets should specifically reduce naming an earlier task; persistent blank answers would suggest an additional barrier.
openings.probe: Ask participants to identify the next task using the current sheet and the dated packet, counterbalancing order. Record earlier-task errors separately from blanks. Then track task identification across six sessions, counting packet creation, printing and replacement effort toward the weekly 90-minute limit.
assumptions: Topics can be fixed six sessions ahead.
Participants retain packets or obtain a replacement.
No preparation or prior attendance becomes an entry requirement.

openings.claim: Unequal topic familiarity may impede conversation entry.
openings.discriminator: Fresh starts improve reciprocal speech, especially with differing familiarity.
openings.probe: Randomly offer consenting pairs usual or equivalent fresh prompts plus one-minute introductions; privately record familiarity, observe individual speaking minutes, collect usefulness and preparation time.
openings.uncertainty: Proficiency and prompt differences remain alternatives; preparation feasibility is unknown.

openings.claim: Current versus earlier task confusion may cause preparation errors.
openings.discriminator: Dated cards reduce earlier-task answers.
openings.probe: Compare existing and dated paper formats privately at handoff; separate earlier answers from blanks, correct misunderstandings, give everyone dated information, and log coordination time.
openings.uncertainty: Immediate identification may not predict later recall.

openings.claim: Optional individual scaffolds and alternating roles may support differing conversational challenge on shared fresh prompts.
openings.discriminator: Useful minutes increase and speaking gaps shrink; balance without usefulness weakens explanation.
openings.probe: Counterbalance usual and supported rounds; use sentence starters/extensions and two six-minute turns before support choice; observe individual speech, collect usefulness/entry slips, log preparation.
openings.uncertainty: Continuous self-calibration is speculative; reliable challenge signals and feasible scaffolds remain dependencies.

openings.claim: Six dated detachable cards may recover preparation continuity after absence without learner tracking.
openings.discriminator: Earlier-task errors fall; persistent blanks indicate another barrier.
openings.probe: Counterbalance current-sheet/packet identification; separate stale answers and blanks, follow six sessions, and count creation, printing and replacement effort.
openings.uncertainty: Requires fixed topics, self-contained tasks, packet retention or available spares.

evidence.decision: Test hypotheses within the valued structure. Remain free; exclude nobody for absence, preparation or refusing public proficiency labels. Use one room, 75 Wednesday minutes, no additional paid facilitation; provide preparation without smartphone/account. Measure conversational practice: six-session targets are 80% reporting ten useful minutes, 85% identifying preparation, coordination below 90 minutes/week. Synthetic, unlinked slips, untimed speech and unknown usefulness definitions limit inference; no target attainment demonstrated.

openings.claim: Preserve the structure; fresh equivalent prompts plus mutual introduction may equalize familiarity and ease entry.
openings.discriminator: Earlier reciprocal speech and more useful minutes, especially with unequal familiarity.
openings.probe: Randomize consenting pairs to usual or fresh prompts plus one-minute introduction; privately record familiarity, observe both speaking times, collect usefulness, log preparation.
openings.uncertainty: Prompt equivalence, proficiency confounding and preparation cost remain unresolved.

openings.claim: Optional starters/extensions and alternating roles may improve entry and turn allocation; continuous calibration additionally requires reliable usefulness feedback.
openings.discriminator: Both partners gain useful minutes and speaking gaps shrink; balanced speech without usefulness weakens the explanation.
openings.probe: Counterbalance usual/supported rounds using comparable fresh prompts; use two six-minute roles then choose support; observe speech, collect usefulness/entry slips, log preparation.
openings.uncertainty: Independent scaffold usability and affordable adaptation are unproven; continuous calibration remains speculative.

openings.claim: A dated paper card may prevent confusion between current and earlier tasks.
openings.discriminator: Fewer earlier-task answers versus existing presentation; distinguish blanks.
openings.probe: Compare consenting attendees' private task/session identification at handoff; correct errors and give everyone dated information; log printing, explanation and messaging.
openings.uncertainty: Immediate identification does not establish later recall.

openings.claim: Six detachable dated cards and spare packets may recover preparation after absence without learner tracking; requires stable topics and self-contained tasks.
openings.discriminator: Earlier-task errors decrease; persistent blanks indicate another barrier.
openings.probe: Counterbalance current-sheet/packet identification; track six sessions and creation, printing, replacement effort.
openings.uncertainty: Advance scheduling, retention/replacement and cost are unproven.

evidence.decision: Test hypotheses; synthetic, untimed, unlinked slips prove no success. Keep participation free, permit absence and private proficiency, provide account-free paper access, retain conversational outcomes. Stop variants exceeding one-room Wednesday 75 minutes, existing unpaid facilitation or 90-minute weekly coordination. Evaluate six-session targets: 80% report ten useful speaking minutes; 85% identify next preparation. Preserve frequent attendees' valued structure.

evidence.title: Sharing rehearsal rooms among amateur music groups
evidence.beneficiary: Amateur music groups sharing a neighborhood arts building and the volunteer who maintains its booking records.
evidence.valued_outcome: Groups obtain usable rehearsal time with predictable access, while the building’s existing rooms and opening hours serve a broad set of participants.
evidence.success_measure: Across eight weeks, at least 90% of groups’ stated rehearsal needs are met within their acceptable time windows, fewer than two access conflicts occur, and booking administration averages no more than two hours per week.

hard_constraints_with_source.text: The building has two rehearsal rooms and may open only during the existing 24 staffed hours per week; no extra staffed hours are funded.
Each participating group must retain access to at least one 60-minute slot weekly if it requests one within any available opening period.
Reservations and changes must remain possible by telephone or in person, without requiring every participant to use a digital account.
The next eight weeks must use the existing room equipment and charge no new participant fees; the two dated public performances already booked must proceed.

changeable_assumptions: Most repeating bookings inherit the same weekday and starting time from the previous season.
The volunteer currently records a reservation against a group name and one contact person.
evidence.incumbent_description: A paper calendar at the building and a volunteer-maintained online copy show 90-minute room bookings. Groups contact the volunteer to reserve or release time and collect room keys from the staffed desk.

supplied_observations.text: Twelve groups made 76 bookings during four weeks. Eleven groups obtained at least one weekly booking; one group reported two weeks without a suitable slot.
The calendars showed 68% of available room-hours reserved. Desk notes indicated that 14 booked sessions started at least 20 minutes late or were not attended.
Nine requests were declined because the requested room and time were booked. Six requested Tuesday or Thursday evenings; acceptable alternatives were not recorded.
Three access conflicts occurred: two calendars disagreed once, and two groups arrived expecting the same room on two other occasions.
One room contains the only acoustic piano. Seven of the 76 bookings specified a piano requirement; equipment needs were blank on the remaining entries.
Administration took 95, 140, 110, and 165 minutes over the observed weeks. Twenty-three changes were communicated through calls or conversations at the desk.
Four groups reported rehearsing elsewhere after an unsuccessful request. Their travel time, outside access arrangements, and total rehearsal needs were not documented.

unmeasured_variables: Acceptable time windows and necessary equipment for each group.
Actual room occupancy, overlap in group membership, and causes of missed or shortened sessions.
available_resources: The volunteer, four weeks of calendars and desk notes, and one contact person from each group available for a short conversation.
evidence.evidence_provenance: authored synthetic case; observations stipulated not real empirical data

evidence.assessment: The incumbent provides recurring reservations, telephone/in-person access and staffed key collection; eleven groups obtained weekly bookings (H4-O1). Its effectiveness is bounded: three conflicts occurred and administration averaged 127.5 minutes/week, while the denominator for 90% needs fulfillment is unknown. H4-O3 supplies a limiting observation: concentrated evening requests mean 68% aggregate reservation utilization does not establish usable spare capacity. H4-O5 further limits interchangeability because only one room has a piano and blank equipment fields cannot establish flexibility. Late or missed sessions are observed, but their causes and recoverability are unmeasured. Neither scheduling nor record errors alone are established as the dominant cause.

openings.claim: Some unmet needs may result from inherited reservations and missing compatibility information rather than insufficient total room-hours.
openings.delta: Test assignment feasibility using acceptable windows, duration and equipment, instead of treating all unreserved hours as substitutable.
openings.prediction: If allocation is the bottleneck, a feasible reassignment will meet previously rejected needs without displacing another group's weekly minimum. If compatible demand exceeds capacity at restricted times or in the piano room, calendar slack will persist without resolving those needs.
openings.probe: Use short contact conversations to record each group's total weekly needs, acceptable windows and necessary equipment. Construct a paper feasibility schedule for the eight weeks, locking public performances and each requested 60-minute weekly minimum; compare fulfilled needs against recorded demand before proposing agreed changes.
assumptions: Contacts can describe group requirements reliably.
Any reassignment requires group agreement and stays within existing rooms, equipment and staffed hours, without fees.

openings.claim: A single authoritative change record with explicit confirmation may reduce conflicting expectations and reconciliation work.
openings.delta: Make each change traceable from request through confirmation and calendar update; distinguish divergent copies from misunderstandings despite matching copies.
openings.prediction: If divergent records dominate, confirmed entries should disagree less across copies and conflicts should fall. Conflicts despite matching records would instead implicate communication or interpretation.
openings.probe: Pilot numbered changes in the existing desk register, read back room/date/time by telephone or in person, and mark online-copy updates. Record conflict circumstances and total weekly administration, including added confirmation work.
assumptions: The existing volunteer and desk can maintain the register within current staffing.
The procedure changes no access entitlement or performance reservation and requires no digital accounts or fees.

evidence.assessment: The observations establish unmet suitable-time requests, access conflicts and variable administrative load, but do not establish whether usable capacity is insufficient. Unrecorded acceptable windows, equipment needs and total rehearsal needs prevent assessment of the 90% target. Both proposed mechanisms remain hypotheses.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: replacing inherited repeating allocations with a needs-based schedule could improve access within existing capacity. Protect the two performances, allocate each requesting group its guaranteed weekly 60 minutes, then allocate additional time against stated needs and acceptable windows.
openings.delta: Allocate room-time from explicitly recorded needs rather than inherited 90-minute reservations; treat piano eligibility as a requirement to establish, not infer from blank records.
openings.prediction: If inherited allocations rather than unavoidable demand concentration explain exclusion, a candidate schedule will meet more stated needs than the incumbent schedule using the same rooms and hours. If no feasible allocation exists after recording alternatives, this mechanism will not establish the target.
openings.probe: Use the available short contact conversations, by telephone or in person, to record weekly duration needs, acceptable windows, equipment and minimum usable session length. Compare incumbent and candidate allocations against that same demand list, explicitly checking weekly guarantees and performance locks before adopting changes.
assumptions: Contacts can specify needs and acceptable alternatives.
A guaranteed 60-minute allocation is not counted as fully meeting a longer rehearsal need.
Feasibility within all fixed constraints remains unproven.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: one authoritative booking ledger with numbered reservations, explicit supersession of changes and room/time readback could reduce conflicting expectations and reconciliation work.
openings.delta: Make telephone and desk requests update one record before confirmation; mark the second calendar with its update time and confirm bookings from the authoritative record.
openings.prediction: Conflicts caused by inconsistent records or unacknowledged changes should decline; conflicts despite matching current confirmations would implicate another cause. Administrative time may increase if recording overhead exceeds saved reconciliation.
openings.probe: During the eight weeks, record conflict causes, confirmation identifiers and total weekly administration minutes. Test the fewer-than-two-conflicts and two-hours-average targets while continuing to measure stated needs met; preserve existing guarantees and performance bookings.
assumptions: The volunteer and desk can consistently consult the authoritative ledger.
Participants can receive confirmations verbally without digital accounts.
Record inconsistency explains only some observed conflicts.

openings.claim: Inherited allocations and missing compatibility information may cause exclusion; needs-based reassignment could improve access.
openings.discriminator: Compare both schedules against identical stated demand: improvement supports allocation effects; infeasible compatible demand indicates restricted-time or piano capacity limits despite 68% reservation utilization.
openings.probe: Converse with contacts by telephone or in person about total weekly needs, acceptable windows, equipment and minimum usable duration, including needs rehearsed elsewhere. Construct an eight-week paper schedule locking performances and weekly guarantees, then allocate additional time; obtain group agreement before changes.
openings.uncertainty: Needs and alternatives are unrecorded; blank equipment entries do not imply flexibility. Contact reliability and feasibility are unproven; 60 minutes cannot satisfy a longer need automatically.

openings.claim: An authoritative ledger with numbered bookings, explicit change supersession and verbal readback may reduce conflicting expectations and reconciliation.
openings.discriminator: Fewer divergent records supports record consistency; conflicts despite matching current confirmations implicate communication or interpretation. Added recording overhead may exceed savings.
openings.probe: Update the desk ledger before confirmation; read back room/date/time, mark online-copy update time, and track confirmation identifiers, conflict circumstances and all administration minutes across eight weeks, alongside needs fulfillment.
openings.uncertainty: Consistent volunteer/desk use is assumed. Record inconsistency explains only some conflicts; staffing feasibility remains unproven.

lineage.reason: Retains compatibility hypothesis and capacity discriminator.
Adds allocation order and duration safeguard.

evidence.decision: Probe both hypotheses; neither dominates established evidence. Preserve two rooms, existing equipment, 24 staffed hours/week, no fees, both dated performances, requested weekly 60-minute access within available opening periods, and telephone/in-person changes without accounts. Eight-week targets: at least 90% stated needs within acceptable windows, fewer than two conflicts, administration averaging at most 120 minutes/week. Baseline: three conflicts, 127.5 minutes/week; fulfillment denominator unknown. Synthetic observations leave actual occupancy, membership overlap and missed-session causes/recoverability unmeasured.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: replace inherited allocations with a needs-based schedule; improvement depends on compatible demand fitting available room-times, including piano requirements.
openings.discriminator: More needs met than incumbent under identical demand supports allocation mismatch; infeasible concentrated demand despite slack limits this mechanism.
openings.probe: Interview contacts by telephone/in person for weekly needs, acceptable windows, equipment and minimum usable duration. Compare incumbent and paper candidate across eight weeks, locking performances and weekly guarantees; seek agreement before changes. Do not count 60 minutes as satisfying longer needs.
openings.uncertainty: Contact reliability and feasibility remain unproven; blank equipment entries establish no flexibility. Stop adoption if constraints fail.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: an authoritative ledger, numbered bookings/changes, explicit supersession and room/date/time readback reduce conflicts and reconciliation if inconsistent records or unacknowledged changes contribute.
openings.discriminator: Fewer copy disagreements and conflicts support record causation; conflicts despite matching current confirmations suggest communication, interpretation or another cause.
openings.probe: Update the desk ledger before verbal confirmation; mark online-copy updates and times. Track identifiers, conflict circumstances and total administration including recording/readback overhead throughout eight weeks.
openings.uncertainty: Volunteer/desk consistency is assumed; added work may exceed reconciliation savings. Neither record errors nor scheduling is established as dominant; missed-session causes/recoverability remain unknown.

lineage.reason: Compatibility feasibility and reassignment gates preserved.
Needs-based operation and comparable-demand test preserved.
Supersession, confirmation order and overhead dependency preserved.

evidence.decision: Test both hypotheses. Preserve two rooms, existing equipment, 24 staffed hours/week, no new fees, both performances, telephone/in-person booking/changes without mandatory digital accounts, and a requested weekly 60-minute slot when any opening is acceptable. Success requires >=90% stated needs within acceptable windows, fewer than two conflicts and <=120 administration minutes/week averaged over eight weeks; the needs denominator is currently unknown.

evidence.title: Community laundry drying rack access
evidence.valued_outcome: Residents can find usable rack space without disturbing another resident's laundry.
evidence.success_measure: During the stipulated busy period, at least nine of ten arrivals locate usable space within three minutes without moving another load.

hard_constraints.text: No resident may move another resident's laundry.
Keep the existing four racks and room layout.
Any per-load recording must take no more than one minute.
Do not record names or apartment numbers.

evidence.incumbent: Residents choose rack space on arrival. Existing partial mechanisms are paper arrival-time tags attached to loads and a wall calendar showing requested drying windows. Tags show when a load was placed, while calendar entries describe intentions. No one routinely reconciles the two.

observations.text: Synthetic arrival log: eight of 20 arrivals initially found all racks occupied.
Synthetic tag audit: seven of 18 tags remained attached after their laundry was removed.
Synthetic calendar sample: five of twelve requested windows had no corresponding arrival.
Synthetic resident diary: three residents described usable space obscured by empty tagged hangers.
Synthetic timing sheet: adding an arrival-time tag took 25 to 45 seconds in six trials.
Synthetic room log: two racks became empty within ten minutes of each other on one evening.

unknowns: How often tags are removed promptly.
Whether planned windows influence actual arrival choices.
resources: Existing tags, calendar, pencils and four racks.
changeable_assumptions: Arrival time is the only load state recorded.
Requested windows are accepted without confirmation.
evidence.provenance: Entirely authored synthetic preservation fixture; supplied sources are stipulations, not field observations or tested effects.

openings.claim: A load-state tag plus confirmation of requested windows may reduce searches: state updates reveal removal while confirmation distinguishes intentions from arrivals.
openings.delta: Connect tag state to confirmed window state instead of interpreting arrival timestamps and unconfirmed calendar entries separately.
openings.prediction: If both records stay current, combined records may reduce searches more than updated tags alone or confirmed windows alone; this is untested.
openings.probe: Compare those three conditions with equal arrival schedules; record search time and recording time. Stop if recording exceeds one minute or identities are required.
assumptions: Residents update removal state.
Confirmation is anonymous and takes little time.

openings.claim: Would removal of an empty hanger's tag, coupled with a visible vacant-space marker, make released capacity easier to identify?
openings.delta: Represent vacancy explicitly rather than infer it from a load timestamp.
openings.prediction: If visual ambiguity causes searches, paired changes may outperform tag removal alone; no effect is established.
openings.probe: Compare paired changes, tag removal alone and existing practice. Stop if markers obscure occupied laundry or require moving another load.
assumptions: Released spaces are otherwise hard to distinguish.
Markers fit existing racks.

openings.claim: Connect load-state tags with confirmed requested windows: removal updates reveal release; anonymous confirmation distinguishes intentions from arrivals. Together they may reduce searches.
openings.discriminator: Current combined records outperform updated tags alone and confirmed windows alone.
