evidence.title: Small museum audio handset return
evidence.beneficiary: Visitors borrowing audio handsets and the reception attendant
evidence.valued_outcome: Visitors receive a ready handset with their selected language at the beginning of a visit.
evidence.success_measure: At least 95% of handoffs during the stipulated entrance period begin playback in the requested language within one minute.

hard_constraints.text: Use the existing twelve handsets and charging dock.
The reception attendant retains responsibility for admission; no added staff.
Do not collect visitor identities or persist listening histories.
Return handling must average no more than 30 seconds per handset.

evidence.incumbent: Returned handsets enter the charging dock and are handed out when their charge indicator is green. Existing partial mechanisms are green charge indicators showing battery readiness and laminated language cards helping visitors select the handset menu. The attendant relies on the preceding visitor's menu state until the next handoff.

observations.text: Synthetic handoff log: nine of 36 green-indicator handsets initially played the preceding visitor's language.
Synthetic timing record: eight of those nine handoffs exceeded one minute.
Synthetic return sample: checking charge alone took an average of eight seconds per handset.
Synthetic visitor tally: language choices were split among three menu options.
Synthetic menu trial: selecting a language from the home screen took 12 to 22 seconds in six trials.
Synthetic dock audit: four green-indicator handsets were sitting on a language submenu rather than the home screen.

unknowns: Whether submenu state contributes independently to delays.
How return timing overlaps with admission queues.
resources: Existing handsets, charging dock, language cards and timing sheet.
changeable_assumptions: Menu state is handled only at the next handoff.
evidence.provenance: Entirely authored synthetic preservation fixture; supplied sources are stipulations, not field observations or tested effects.

openings.claim: A return-to-home-screen step coupled with a visitor language choice before handoff could remove inherited language state and shorten menu navigation.
openings.delta: Treat menu readiness and requested language as joint handoff conditions alongside battery readiness.
openings.prediction: If inherited menu state causes delays, the pair may outperform resetting alone or advance choice alone; effects remain untested.
openings.probe: Compare paired steps, each step alone and existing practice across matched language requests. Stop if return handling exceeds 30 seconds on average.
assumptions: Reset returns reliably to the home screen.
Choice can be communicated without retaining visitor data.

openings.claim: Language-specific dock positions plus a visible menu-state check might reduce wrong-language handoffs by aligning location cues with actual settings.
openings.delta: Use location and verified setting together instead of charge indication as the availability cue.
openings.prediction: If location cues remain accurate, the pair may outperform dock grouping alone; uneven language demand could erase the benefit.
openings.probe: Compare paired steps with grouping alone under equal and uneven demand. Stop if admission work is delayed or visitor history is retained.
assumptions: Dock positions can be marked without replacement.
Setting checks do not consume admission capacity.

openings.claim: Return to the home screen and obtain the visitor's language choice before handoff; require menu state, requested language and battery readiness jointly.
openings.discriminator: The paired steps may outperform either alone if inherited menu state causes delays: synthetically, nine of 36 green handsets played the previous language and eight exceeded one minute.
openings.probe: Compare paired steps, reset alone, advance choice alone and existing practice across matched requests. Measure requested-language playback within one minute and average return time; stop above 30 seconds.
openings.uncertainty: Untested effects; reset reliability, reset impact on charge indication, independent submenu contribution and queue overlap remain unknown. Choice must be communicated without retaining visitor data. Synthetic home-screen selection took 12–22 seconds; charge-only returns averaged eight seconds.

openings.claim: Combine language-specific positions in the existing dock with a visible check of actual menu settings; location and verified setting jointly supplement charge readiness.
openings.discriminator: The pair may outperform grouping alone when location cues remain accurate. Uneven demand could erase benefits; synthetic choices spanned three options and four green handsets remained on submenus.
openings.probe: Compare paired steps with grouping alone under equal and uneven demand. Measure handoff success, return time and admission interference; stop if admission is delayed or histories retained.
openings.uncertainty: Dock marking feasibility, cue accuracy and setting checks' admission capacity cost are untested.

lineage.reason: Preserves paired readiness conditions and separate-step comparisons.
Preserves location-setting conjunction and demand dependence.

evidence.decision: Both are probe candidates, supported only by synthetic stipulations. Require at least 95% requested-language playback within one minute during the stipulated entrance period. Preserve twelve handsets and dock, admission responsibility with the existing attendant, no visitor identities or persisted histories, and average returns no longer than 30 seconds.

openings.claim: Return to home screen plus communicated visitor language choice makes menu state, requested language and battery joint readiness conditions; removing inherited state and shortening navigation depends on reliable reset and selection.
openings.discriminator: Pair outperforms reset alone, choice alone and incumbent on matched requests if inherited state causes delays.
openings.probe: Compare all four conditions; measure correct-language playback within 60 seconds and average return time. Stop above 30 seconds; check reset effects on charge indication and admission overlap.
openings.uncertainty: Untested synthetic evidence; independent submenu effect, reset reliability, charge-indicator effects and queue overlap unknown. Choice must remain transient.

openings.claim: Language-specific dock positions plus visible setting checks align location cues with actual menu settings; fewer wrong-language handoffs depends on accurate cues and admission capacity.
openings.discriminator: Pair beats grouping alone under equal and uneven language demand; uneven demand could erase benefit.
openings.probe: Compare pair with grouping alone under both demand patterns; measure language errors, timely playback and return time. Stop for delayed admission, retained history or mean returns above 30 seconds.
openings.uncertainty: Untested; marking existing dock positions and checking settings without consuming admission capacity remain assumptions.

lineage.reason: Paired dependency, component comparisons and return-time gate preserved.
Cue-verification dependency, uneven-demand test and admission/privacy gates preserved.

evidence.decision: Retain both as separate untested candidates. Require existing twelve handsets/dock, no added staff, attendant admission responsibility, no identities or persisted listening histories, and mean return handling at most 30 seconds. Target at least 95% correct-language playback within one minute during stipulated entrance period; synthetic fixtures establish no effects.
